definition: A staging area in CPU memory where data lands before being copied on to its real destination (for example from a NIC or SSD into GPU memory). Each bounce costs host memory bandwidth, CPU time and latency; GPUDirect removes it.
The command protocol flash SSDs use over PCIe. It allows tens of thousands of parallel queues, which is why one modern SSD can deliver several GB/s.
NVMe commands carried over a network (RDMA, TCP or Fibre Channel) so a server can use remote flash as if it were a local drive. DPUs can run the initiator or target in hardware.

The share of a server's CPU cycles spent on the provider's plumbing (virtual switching, storage protocols, encryption, telemetry, management) rather than the customer's work. Published estimates cluster around 19-33%; also called the datacenter tax.

Software (for example Open vSwitch, OVS) that forwards packets between virtual machines or containers and the physical network, applying tenant rules. Running it on the host costs CPU cores; a DPU runs it in hardware.
A virtual network for each tenant built on top of the physical one by wrapping packets in an outer header (for example VXLAN), so many customers can share the same switches without seeing each other.
Several customers sharing the same physical infrastructure while being kept isolated from one another in performance, network reachability and data.

A cloud server rented with no provider hypervisor underneath: the tenant controls the whole operating system. The provider's control software must then live somewhere the tenant cannot reach, such as a DPU.
A security design in which no component (including the host OS) is trusted by default; every access is authenticated and policy is enforced outside the tenant's control, for example on a DPU.
A standard for encrypting and authenticating network traffic at the IP layer. Doing it in software at hundreds of Gb/s consumes many CPU cores; DPUs and NICs encrypt inline.
Continuous measurement of flows, congestion, errors and latency inside the network and NICs, used to find stragglers and tune congestion control.
A chip that fans one PCIe connection out to several devices (GPUs, NICs, SSDs) and lets them exchange data peer-to-peer without going through the CPU. ConnectX-8 builds one in.
A hardware-isolated region (a confidential VM on the CPU, a GPU in confidential mode) whose memory and state the host OS, hypervisor and cloud operator cannot read or alter.
Cryptographic proof, signed by keys burned into the chip, that a TEE is genuine hardware running approved firmware and settings. A customer checks it before sending secrets such as model weights.
A small, immutable security block on a chip that holds identity keys and verifies firmware at boot; everything else in the chain of trust is checked against it.

PCI-SIG's TEE Device Interface Security Protocol: a standard way to bring a PCIe device (GPU, NIC, SSD) inside a CPU's confidential VM with authenticated, encrypted links instead of software bounce buffers.

AMD's confidential-VM technology for EPYC CPUs (Secure Encrypted Virtualization with Secure Nested Paging): encrypts each VM's memory and blocks the hypervisor from tampering. SEV-TIO extends it to PCIe devices via TDISP.
Intel Trust Domain Extensions: Intel's confidential-VM technology for Xeon CPUs. TDX Connect extends it to PCIe devices via TDISP.
Arm Confidential Compute Architecture: Armv9 'Realms' that isolate a VM from the host software, Arm's counterpart to SEV-SNP and TDX.

A file system that stripes each file across many storage servers so thousands of clients can read and write at once (for example Lustre/DDN EXAScaler, IBM Storage Scale, WEKA). Suited to checkpoints and training I/O.
Storage that keeps data as whole objects addressed by key over HTTP (S3 API), scaling to exabytes cheaply but with higher latency than a parallel file system; usually holds raw datasets and archives.
Placing data on a ladder of memories, from small and fast (HBM) to large and slow (shared flash), and moving it up and down as it is needed; NVIDIA labels KV-cache tiers G1 to G4.
